big_case.notes: Routine federal-employee FTCA/FECA primary-jurisdiction dispute arising from an unpublished motions-panel summary affirmance after the petitioner declined to file a FECA claim during a district-court stay, with the Government waiving its response and the Court denying certiorari without comment on the first conference order list.

central_claims.claim: The Court will deny the petition for a writ of certiorari without comment on the first order list following the November 6, 2026 conference, with zero relists.
The Court will not issue a Call for the Views of the Solicitor General (CVSG) because the federal respondents are already represented by the Solicitor General, who waived a response.
No Justice will note a dissent or file a separate statement respecting the denial of certiorari.

central_claims.basis: Certiorari was denied, so conditional grant and route predictions were not tested by the outcome.
central_claims.claim: Conditional on a grant, the Court would take the single question presented on whether 5 U.S.C. §§ 8116(c) and 8128(b) require district courts to stay FTCA claims whenever a substantial question of FECA coverage exists, and resolve it via plenary merits review rather than summary disposition.
